facts.text: Buddhist temple in Tianning District, Changzhou, with the 13-storey Tianning Pagoda, 153.79 m tall, completed 2007 and described as the tallest pagoda in the world.
The temple grounds date back to the Tang dynasty; the current pagoda was finished in April 2007.
Located at 636 Yanling Middle Road, a few hundred metres east of the Culture Palace metro station.

facts.text: Theme park in Changzhou, open since September 2000, covering more than 600 mu (0.27 km2), also called the Eastern Jurassic Park.
Its museum holds a nearly complete Sinosauropteryx fossil skeleton plus Brachiosaurus and Hadrosaurus fossils.
Rides, dancing dinosaurs and a few fossils; at 1 Hanjiang Road, Xinbei District.

facts.text: Remains of an ancient Spring and Autumn period city, now rebuilt and displayed as a tourist attraction rated AAAAA, the highest official rating.
Yancheng is a city enclosed by three concentric moats (three cities, three rivers), about 850 m east-west and 750 m north-south, some 2,500 years old.
Wooden dugout canoes were unearthed at the site in 1958; two are held in the Wujin Yancheng Museum.
The Chunqiu Yancheng tourist area comprises the ruins park, the Spring and Autumn amusement park, the wild animal world and a traditional commercial street.

facts.text: Hongmei (Red Plum) Park, in northeast Changzhou, is one of the city's largest comprehensive parks at 37 hectares, with gardens and a lake.
At the rear are the Writing Pagoda (Wenbi Ta) and Red Plum Pavilion; also a flamingo pond and elevated walkway among trees.
Open all day and free to enter.

facts.text: Small 2.667-hectare Grand Canal park named for the Song poet Su Dongpo, who is commemorated by a boat-fitting pavilion where he once boated.
Appears like an island, bounded by the Grand Canal and smaller canals; an islet joined by an arching bridge has a Dongpo academy hall fronted by his statue.
The main garden holds the foundations and carved-stone fragments of a palace built for Emperor Qianlong's visit.

facts.text: Creative campus at 141 Sanbao Street, Zhonglou District, founded in late 2008 on 36,388 m2 with about 32,000 m2 of floor area.
A former textile mill on the Grand Canal turned into art studios, restaurants, nightclubs and museums, with the old buildings preserved.
A tour boat runs here from Dongpo Park.

facts.text: Comprehensive museum founded 1958 with more than 20,000 relics in eight sections, including Spring and Autumn green porcelain, Song and Yuan lacquerware and porcelain, and Ming and Qing paintings.
The current building west of People's Square opened to the public on 28 April 2007.
At 1288 Longcheng Avenue; entry is free, English guides are available for CNY 100.

facts.text: Wild animal park in Wujin District, Changzhou, with walk-through and drive-through areas; visitors may drive their own vehicle through the park.
Part of the Chunqiu Yancheng AAAAA tourist area; at 199 Wuyi Middle Road, Wujin.
Wikipedia notes the zoo has been described as open only in spring and autumn; the official page gives no seasonal closure (this conflict is unresolved).

facts.text: Lake 8 km south of Liyang, listed as a provincial tourist resort in 1993 and graded AAAA nature reserve in 2001 (now operated as the Tianmu Lake scenic area).
The scenic area offers boat trips on the lake (the Shanshuiyuan ticket includes the boat).
Sits by Nanshan Bamboo Sea, run by the same operator, which is also a 5A scenic area.

facts.text: Ecological tourist area in the southern mountains of Liyang, open since 2000, near Tianmu Lake.
About 2,300 hectares of bamboo make up the 'bamboo sea'.
Zones include a lake entertainment district, a historic area and a mountaineering area; a ground cable car runs (service notices on the operator site).
